subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should stale auto-sourced literal `openai` session route state be owned by the OpenAI provider doctor contract, the Codex app-server doctor contract, or a generic stale-auto fallback repair path?
rationale: Literal `openai` is the canonical OpenAI provider id, while OpenAI agent turns may run through the Codex app-server runtime; automation should not choose that ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex ownership focused on runtime ids and legacy aliases, with tests guarding auto-only cleanup.

options.title: Codex owns app-server OpenAI state
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers define OpenAI agent turns as Codex-owned for session route repair.

options.title: Make stale-auto cleanup generic
options.body: Move repair classification out of provider-specific ownership when an auto override no longer matches the configured route, while keeping explicit/user choices manual.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex ownership focused on runtime ids and legacy aliases, with tests guarding auto-only cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest prior merged history on the doctor/Codex route-state repair direction and is the clearest owner-boundary decision candidate.
